title: How to Tell if a PDF Has Been Edited: Six Things to Inspect
summary: How to tell if a PDF has been edited using document properties, dates, producer fields, saves, signatures, and fonts, and why each can mislead.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** To tell if a PDF has been edited, open Document Properties, compare the created and modified dates, read the producer field and font list, then check the file's save history and any digital signature. None of these proves an edit alone, because printing to PDF, scanning, compression, and form filling leave similar marks. Signature panels need care too: a 2018 evaluation found 21 of 22 desktop PDF viewers vulnerable to at least one signature attack before coordinated disclosure led vendors to work on fixes.


## What an Ordinary Reader Can Actually See


A PDF viewer can reveal much of a file's recorded history without special software. Two kinds of fake need separating first. An edited-after-creation file began as a genuine document, and someone changed it later. A generated-from-scratch file has no genuine original, so it may show no sign of editing at all.[Detecting an AI-generated PDF](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-detect-ai-generated-pdf) is a different exercise, and a clean edit history says nothing about it.


[Cotality's 2026 fraud report](https://www.cotality.com/reports/2026-annual-fraud-report) estimated that 1 in 119 US mortgage applications carried indications of fraud in Q2 2026, and it warned that AI has made altered documents harder to identify. Looking closely at the page is no longer enough, so the inspection moves to the file.


Work on a copy of the file. Keep the original untouched, and close any editor without saving, because a save can change the very fields under review. The deeper field-by-field reference is in[PDF metadata analysis](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/pdf-metadata-analysis-fraud-detection) .


## Six Things to Inspect, and How to Read Them


### 1. Document Properties


In Adobe Acrobat or Reader, Ctrl+D or Cmd+D opens Document Properties. The Description tab shows the title, author, Created, Modified, Application, and PDF Producer, and other viewers offer similar panels under their own labels. Read the panel as a set of claims the file makes about itself. Under ISO 32000-1, these fields are optional, and the[PDF Association's forensics presentation](https://pdfa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/0-2-15_30-CherieEkholm-PDF_Forensics_and_the_Metadata_conundrum.pdf) describes them as easily editable. A blank field proves nothing either way.


### 2. Created Versus Modified Dates


Matching or near-matching dates suit a file written once. A Modified date well after Created means something wrote to the file again. Compare both dates with the date printed on the document and the date the file arrived. A March statement created in early April fits. A March statement created in September, then modified minutes before submission, needs an explanation.


Dates mislead in both directions. A later Modified date often reflects a form fill or a signature. Matching dates can belong to a brand-new file created by printing an already altered document. Both values also depend on the software and clock that wrote them.


### 3. Application and PDF Producer


ISO 32000-1 defines Creator as the product that made the original document before conversion, and Producer as the product that converted it to PDF. Acrobat displays these as Application and PDF Producer. Ask whether the pair fits the issuer, ideally by comparing a known-genuine file of the same type from the same institution. A payroll export whose producer names a consumer editing product deserves a question.


The same PDF Association presentation recommends that editing tools leave the original creator in place and update the producer. That is a recommendation, and software does not follow it uniformly. A producer that fits the issuer does not show the file is unchanged, and one that does not fit may reflect an accountant's merge or a scanning workstation.


### 4. Incremental Saves


ISO 32000 lets software save changes by appending them to the end of a file, leaving the earlier bytes in place. The viewer shows only the latest result. To look for appended sections, open a copy in a plain text editor and search for the marker %%EOF. The[PDF Association's incremental save guide](https://pdfa.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/1-3-11_00-CherieEkholm-In_Defence_of_Incremental_Saves.pdf) lists this marker and the Prev key as the starting points. More than one marker suggests more than one section.


The count needs interpretation. Linearized files, which Acrobat reports as Fast Web View: Yes, can resemble an incremental save without being one. Form filling, annotations, signatures, and changes with no visual effect also create new sections. A single marker does not clear the file either, because many tools write a full save that carries no earlier version forward. The count says that a file changed more than once. It does not say what changed.


### 5. Signature Validity Panel


A digital signature is the strongest of these checks where one exists. An image of a signature on the page is not one.[Adobe's validation guide](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/e-sign-documents/manage-digital-signatures/validate-digital-sign.html) explains how to open the Signatures panel and review the signer's certificate. Acrobat also offers View Signed Version and Compare Signed Version to Current Version, which show what the signature covered and what came afterward.


Read the status precisely. A changes-after-signing message is routine when a second person signs or completes a permitted field, and the comparison shows whether the change matters. An unknown status often points to a certificate the viewer does not trust, a separate issue from tampering. Signature time can come from the signer's computer clock unless a trusted timestamp was used. A valid signature shows that the signed bytes are intact and says nothing about whether the content was true when signed.


Viewer software is also part of the check. The[PDF Insecurity research](https://www.pdf-insecurity.org/signature/evaluation_2018.html) found the 21-of-22 result among desktop viewers tested in 2018, so reviewers should use a current, patched viewer for this step.


### 6. The Font List


The Fonts tab in Document Properties lists the fonts used and how they are stored. An entry marked Embedded Subset is normal, and a six-character prefix before the font name is simply how subset fonts are labeled. Compare the list with a known-genuine sample. A face that does not belong to the issuer's usual output is worth following up, as is a figure that looks subtly different from its neighbors at high zoom.


The list applies to the document as a whole, so it cannot say which line used which font. Letterheads, appended pages, and text recognition layers can all add fonts legitimately. A purely scanned page may list no fonts at all.


## Why Each Signal Misleads on Its Own


Knowing how to tell if a document has been altered comes down to corroboration, because ordinary handling produces most of the same marks as tampering. These routine events are the usual explanations a reviewer should rule out.


Routine event What it changes Why it misleads


Print to PDF New dates and producer, with earlier history and signatures gone Hides prior edits and looks like a clean new file


Scanning Scanner software in the producer field, with page images replacing text Font and save checks have little left to read


Compression or optimization Modified date and producer may change, and images may be recompressed Looks like a post-creation edit with no content change


Form filling or signing Later Modified date and appended sections Normal workflow that resembles an incremental edit


Legitimate re-save or merge Modified date, producer, and font mix can shift An accountant or broker may have combined files honestly


Print-to-PDF files deserve particular caution, since[a re-rendered copy behaves much like a screenshot](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/screenshot-vs-original-pdf-document-verification) .


Weigh signals together, against the claimed issuer and the workflow that should have produced the file. An issuer-style producer with one later save may be a form fill. The same save, a mismatched font near a salary figure, and a modification minutes before upload form a pattern that needs an answer.


## What to Do With a Suspect File


Escalate when the evidence touches something that matters. Common triggers include an invalid signature, a signed version that differs from the current one in a material field, a producer that cannot belong to the issuer, several appended sections with no workflow to explain them, or a submitter who cannot say how the file was handled.


Keep the original bytes and record what each panel showed. Ask for a fresh export sent directly from the issuer's portal, then compare the two files. Contact the issuer through details found independently, never through a phone number or link printed on the document. To read the history of a file at the object level, run it through the[Watchdoc playground](https://sphinxhq.com/products/doc-fraud) or hand it to a forensic examiner.


File inspection has a hard limit. It describes how the PDF was made and changed, and it cannot prove the income, payment, or shipment on the page was real. Only the issuer, the payer, or another independent record can confirm that.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How can someone tell if a document has been altered?


For a PDF, compare the created and modified dates, the producer, the font list, the number of saved sections, and any digital signature, then compare those results with a known-genuine file from the same issuer. No single sign is conclusive. The issuer can confirm whether the contents match its records.


### Does a modified date later than the created date mean a PDF was tampered with?


No. Form filling, signing, compression, and ordinary re-saving can all update the modified date. The later date means the file was written again, so the useful follow-up is what changed and who handled the file.


### Does a valid digital signature mean a PDF has not been edited?


A valid signature means the bytes covered by that signature are intact when checked in a current, trusted viewer. Content can still be added after signing, so reviewers should read any changes-after-signing message and compare the signed version with the current one. The signature does not establish that the signed statements were true.


### Can a PDF be changed without leaving visible traces?


Yes. Properties can be absent or rewritten, and many ordinary tools produce a full save that carries no earlier versions. A file with no visible signs of editing is not thereby proven genuine, which is why outside confirmation matters for material decisions.


### Does a PDF keep its edit history?


Only sometimes. Incremental saves keep earlier bytes in the file, and signed documents let a viewer display the version that was signed. Other saves replace the prior structure, so a missing history proves little.
